Replay

Wave pacing and compatibility

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Values, rollback and capacityExisting savesComparison scope

The active-floor director follows the original game's timing at 20 Hz. A new floor starts with wave zero. Its first active tick announces wave one; spawning starts on the following tick, one dweller per tick. Completing a wave means both all scheduled spawns and all live dwellers are gone. The last actual death starts the authored rest, including the final wave's rest. The next wave is announced when that deadline is reached and begins spawning on the following tick.

An empty wave has no death to start a rest, so it advances on the next director call. A started director continues if players temporarily disconnect. A direct server with no started party waits for its first connected player before announcing wave one. Each new floor resets den selection to Den1 and alternates thereafter.

Before C4, Replay waited 20 ticks for its first spawn, then ten ticks between spawns, invented rest periods for empty waves, paused the running director when everyone left and carried the den cursor across floors. Those behaviors did not match the original kit/ai director and Cavecrawl host wiring. Replay's implementation remains independent of Kit; only the oracle imports Kit.

Values, rollback and capacity#

The director stays wholly inside World. Its existing next_spawn field also retains a pending deadline imported from an older save. The corrected pacing emits one spawn per invocation; the game calls the director once per simulation tick. Announcement/remaining/live counts, rest deadlines, entity generations and den selection all participate in replay. A death near u64 exhaustion cannot wrap its rest deadline: it aborts the staged step, preserving the prior committed world.

The fixed dweller pool still holds 16 living entities. If it is full, a pending spawn stays pending until space is freed. The original uses dynamic entities, so custom waves that exceed this simultaneous population do not have identical spawn pacing. Definition limits, collision/AI behavior and unrelated combat rules are unchanged by this increment.

Existing saves#

C4 introduced the corrected director simulation. The server-motion profile uses content C9 (0x4341564552504c39), retaining the avatar transition rules and relic lifetime. C8 introduced authority observation fields; network/checkpoint protocol versions are unchanged. Update both the game and coordinated service before opening a room. Ordinary loads require matching content.

The C1–C7 paths in tools/upgrade_save use frozen source descriptors and require a new destination. See the current conversion guide for the complete accepted format list. C3 conversion retains every frame and session value, including live dwellers, current wave, den cursor, and pending spawn/rest deadlines. Once those deadlines are reached, subsequent spawns use the corrected cadence; a later floor starts from the corrected fresh-floor state. A waiting lobby starts fresh when Start is accepted. This does not reproduce the old timing indefinitely, convert original Kit saves, publish a Room save or grant a new authority lease.

Tests retain real pre-change C3 waiting/pending/spawning/rest archives plus their producer/model hashes. All six C1/C2/C3 fixture conversions resume in fresh native Godot processes with exact converted-frame hashes and a newer local epoch.

Comparison scope#

The oracle executes the unchanged original director beside Replay's real director and rock-death handling. Six named scenarios plus 256 generated wave/rest/death plans compare announcement, spawn ticks, pending/live counts, active rest time, completion and den counts for 1,000 ticks each. The same corpus runs natively and in freestanding WASM. Unit tests cover pool saturation, floor den reset, death/rest input revision and overflow rollback. Normal/faulted full-game campaigns still require 12 slain dwellers, eight gems, both death paths, two floors and a common victory-frame hash.

This is director timing evidence, not full-game parity. C5 fixes the previously recorded avatar-vitals/cooldown discrepancy and C6 corrects relic floor lifetime. Navigation, owner-streamed movement and broader visual/human comparisons remain separate work.
